hints: Write both relevant areas in radians: a sector has area $\tfrac12r^2$ times its angle.
The major-sector angle is $2\pi-x$, while the shaded segment is the minor sector minus its isosceles triangle.
Use segment area $\tfrac12r^2x-\tfrac12r^2\sin x$ in the condition that the major sector has three times this area.
Cancel $\tfrac12r^2$ and rearrange to the required fixed-point form.
walkthrough:
Determine the angle of the major sector:
The minor sector has angle $x$ radians, so the major sector has angle $(2\pi - x)$ radians.

Write the formula for the area of the major sector:
$$\text{Area of major sector} = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2(2\pi - x)$$

Write the formula for the area of the shaded segment:
$$\text{Area of shaded segment} = \text{Area of minor sector} - \text{Area of triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2 x - \dfrac{1}{2}r^2\sin x = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2(x - \sin x)$$

Set up the given condition that the area of the major sector is 3 times the area of the shaded segment:
$$\dfrac{1}{2}r^2(2\pi - x) = 3\left[\dfrac{1}{2}r^2(x - \sin x)\right]$$

Divide both sides by $\dfrac{1}{2}r^2$ (since $r > 0$):
$$2\pi - x = 3(x - \sin x)$$
$$2\pi - x = 3x - 3\sin x$$

Rearrange the equation to isolate $x$:
$$2\pi + 3\sin x = 3x + x$$
$$4x = 3\sin x + 2\pi$$

Divide both sides by 4 to obtain the required equation:
$$x = \dfrac{3}{4}\sin x + \dfrac{2\pi}{4}$$
$$x = \dfrac{3}{4}\sin x + \dfrac{1}{2}\pi$$

hints: Put the equation into zero form, for example $f(x)=x-\tfrac34\sin x-\tfrac12\pi$.
Show that the values have opposite signs and invoke continuity to locate a root between the endpoints.
walkthrough:
Rearrange the equation into the form $f(x) = 0$:
$$f(x) = x - \dfrac{3}{4}\sin x - \dfrac{1}{2}\pi$$

Conclude the sign change argument:
Since $f(x)$ is continuous and changes sign between $x = 2$ ($f(2) < 0$) and $x = 2.5$ ($f(2.5) > 0$), there is at least one root of the equation lying between $2$ and $2.5$.

hints: Use the equation from part (a) directly as $x_{n+1}=\tfrac34\sin x_n+\tfrac12\pi$.
Choose a starting value in the bracket $2<x<2.5$ and calculate successive values in radians.
Record every iterate to 4 decimal places until successive values settle sufficiently to justify rounding the root to 2 decimal places.
walkthrough:
State the iterative formula based on the equation from part (a):
$$x_{n+1} = \dfrac{3}{4}\sin x_n + \dfrac{1}{2}\pi$$

Choose starting value $x_1 = 2$ and evaluate subsequent iterations to 4 decimal places in radians:
$$x_2 = \dfrac{3}{4}\sin(2) + \dfrac{1}{2}\pi = 0.681973 + 1.570796 = 2.2528$$

Round the root to 2 decimal places:
$$x = 2.18$$
